subject: On-prem performance surge: sustained p99/p95 spikes and 502s — urgent tuning & edge config request
messages:
From: Claire Robinson <claire@medtrax.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@medtrax.com, procurement@medtrax.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:07:12 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden p99 spikes and growing 502s on our on‑prem cluster

Hi Laura,

We started seeing sustained tail latency (p99 ~2.4s, p95 ~1.1s) and a rising 502 error rate (~3% from baseline 0.2%) on our MedTrax private instance (medtrax-prod-onprem-1) starting ~02:00 UTC yesterday. This is affecting billing and some inference-backed claims routes and causing timeouts for downstream systems.

Attached a heapdump and the last 6 hours of traces. Ops suspects the nightly batch overlap but we don’t have enough signal to be sure. Can Redwood take an urgent look? This is customer-impacting and the CTO is asking for an explanation and an ETA for mitigation.

Claire Robinson
CTO Office, MedTrax Systems
claire@medtrax.com

Folks — looping you in. MedTrax reported a sustained tail-latency and 502s on their private on‑prem deployment (medtrax-prod-onprem-1). Key asks: (1) triage root cause, (2) short-term mitigation we can propose to the customer within 60–90 mins, (3) a recommended tuning change for their edge/router and runtime that we can roll with minimal risk.

Initial notes: customer says problem started ~02:00 UTC yesterday and they attached traces + heapdump. Ops suspects nightly batch overlap but there are also signs of KV cache growth. Markus / Priyom — can you prioritise a quick infra check (disk/io, CPU steal, NIC errors) and a runtime hot-path trace? Jonas — I’ll need an exec-facing summary once we have recommended mitigations. Olga — please prep a short TSAT for the customer and collect any consent for us to push a non-breaking runtime flag if needed.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Lead, Enterprise — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 10:02:34 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 spikes and growing 502s on our on‑prem cluster

Laura / team — quick findings from a first pass against the traces and the KV stats attached by MedTrax:
- KV cache size has grown ~4x compared to last week for the same QPS, which is increasing GC/eviction churn.
- We see tail latency correlation with a nightly batch window (01:45–03:30 UTC) that overlaps peak inference traffic for certain endpoints.
- Several worker processes are showing increased context switches and syscalls; kernel count for epoll_wait is higher than normal.

Short-term mitigations we can push now (low-risk):
1) Increase worker thread cap on the local serving process by +20% (runtime flag) — minimal restart window (rolling).
2) Enable prefix/KV pre-warm for the top 10 heavy keys for 30 minutes prior to the nightly batch (config flip).
3) Temporarily reduce batch aggregation window to favour latency vs throughput for critical routes.

I’ll run a targeted canary for the worker-thread change on one shard (10% traffic). If green in 15–20 minutes, we can roll. I’ll also attach the deltas we’d apply.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
SRE/Platform, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 12:05:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 spikes and growing 502s on our on‑prem cluster

Adding runtime context — I examined the runtime traces and kernel selection logs from the attached traces:
- There’s a repeated kernel mismatch warning on the quantized path for the re-ranker model; it’s causing fallback to a slower execution path intermittently which amplifies tail latency when the KV cache is under pressure.
- Evidence of GC amplification when the KV cache fills; compaction cycles line up with 502 spikes.

Recommended next steps (medium risk / high impact):
- Deploy a non-invasive runtime flag to prefer the stable kernel path (forces the older path with better latency under pressure) — no model changes needed; quick rollback.
- Tune quantization flags for the re-ranker on medtrax cluster (we can push a conservative profile).
- If latency remains high, propose routing ~20% of traffic to a pre-warmed Dedicated variant for the critical billing endpoints as a short-term fallthrough.

I’ll prepare the flag patch and the rollout script. Priyom — coordinate canary schedule.

Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
markus.klein@redwood.com
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 13:04:20 -07:00
Subject: Exec note: MedTrax on‑prem surge — mitigation & customer ask

Team — quick executive summary for the leadership thread / for MedTrax CTO:
- Situation: MedTrax private instance (medtrax-prod-onprem-1) is experiencing sustained tail-latency (p99 spikes) and ~3% 502s since 02:00 UTC 3/14. Impact: billing and claims workflows intermittently failing.
- Probable causes: KV cache growth + quantized-kernel fallback path under memory pressure + nightly batch overlap.
- Immediate actions accepted: 1) Priyom to canary worker-thread cap increase and batch window reduction (15–30m canary); 2) Markus to push runtime kernel-stability flag (10% shard canary); 3) Offer customer short-term routing of 20% critical billing traffic to pre-warmed Dedicated nodes if needed.
- Ask to Sales/Customer Success (Laura/Olga): prepare an exec-facing note and proposed credits (recommendation: 30% credit on affected invoices for the incident window if we fail to meet the SLA after mitigation).

I’ll be on the 15:30 standup to approve the credit and any emergency Dedicated routing — keep me posted.

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Claire Robinson <claire@medtrax.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 spikes and growing 502s on our on‑prem cluster

Claire — thanks for the report and the heapdump. Quick update and next steps from Redwood: 

What we did (today):
- Ran a 10% shard canary to increase worker-thread cap and reduce batch aggregation window — initial telemetry is promising, p95 improved ~18% on the canary shard and error rate dropped from 3.1% to 0.9% on that shard.
- Deployed a conservative runtime flag to prefer the stable kernel path for the re-ranker (10% shard canary). No model artifacts were changed; this is a config flag and fully reversible.
- Collected additional traces and KV stats (attached: redwood-traces-since-03-14.log, medtrax-prod-kv-stats.csv).

Next steps:
1) If the two canaries remain green for the next 30 minutes we will roll the fixes across the remaining shards in a controlled, rolling manner.
2) If tail-latency or 502s persist after the roll, we will activate a short-term route: move 20% of critical billing traffic to pre-warmed Dedicated capacity while we perform deeper tuning. This requires quick approval from MedTrax to modify routing.
3) Laura will send the exec summary and credit proposal; Jonas has offered to sign off on a 30% invoice credit if we miss SLA after remediation.

Can you confirm we have permission to (a) apply the rolling config changes on medtrax-prod-onprem-1, and (b) route 20% of billing traffic to Redwood Dedicated if we need to? We can do (a) immediately; (b) is only if remediation doesn’t fully resolve.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
